s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty with mastication
Numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement
3-month history of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma
Anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements
Low serum zinc level
Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands on biopsy
Negative direct immunofluorescence test
Negative Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab

shortlist.label: Scurvy
shortlist.why_kept: Low serum zinc level and clinical presentation of painful skin lesions and ulcers

shortlist.label: Zinc deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Low serum zinc level and clinical presentation of skin lesions and ulcers

shortlist.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive painful blisters and ulcers, although negative direct immunofluorescence test

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and clinical presentation of skin lesions and ulcers

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of painful blisters and ulcers, along with a low serum zinc level and other symptoms such as glossitis and hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate, are consistent with scurvy, which is caused by vitamin C deficiency. The patient's history of taking folic acid and cyanocobalamin supplements but no mention of vitamin C supplementation supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Zinc deficiency
rejected.why: While the patient has a low serum zinc level, zinc deficiency does not fully explain the range of symptoms, particularly the specific skin and mucous membrane findings.

rejected.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
rejected.why: The negative direct immunofluorescence test and the presence of subepidermal blisters with eosinophilic bands do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The biopsy findings and negative direct immunofluorescence test do not align with bullous pemphigoid, which typically shows linear IgG and C3 deposition along the basement membrane zone.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of multiple myeloma, the specific symptoms and biopsy findings do not support amyloidosis as the primary diagnosis for the current presentation.
